chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Jazzaki, who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who married a virgin girl, so he found her to be non-virgin (previously married). Is the full dower obligatory for her, or is it reduced? He said: It is reduced.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the dower if a man marries a virgin but finds she is not?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the financial compensation in cases of marital deception (*ghurur*), ruling that the dower (*mahr*) is reduced rather than paid in full when a virginity stipulation is breached. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the dower is linked to the specific qualities agreed upon, ensuring fairness in contractual obligations. It serves as a foundational precedent for modern applications of *khayarat* (options) in marriage contracts regarding physical attributes.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Muhammad Bin Jazzaki who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who married a virgin girl, so he found her as having been married before, and for her is the dower. Should he be loyal (to the dower) or reduced (amount)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Reduced’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja’far from Muhammad ibn Jazzak who has said the following:

“I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked about the case of a man who married a virgin girl but found out that she was not virgin if it was obligatory to pay complete mahr (dower) or less. He (the Imam) answered, ‘It is less.’”
